compensating.why: hop 2 reads the given scope instead of the root of the chain for the global step
hop 2 climbs only one level for the global step
hop 4 starts the local search at the enclosing scope's parent

ownership_reason: Only the gold walks the enclosing local scopes and chooses among their declarations. Hop 1 consults only the scope's own table (an own declaration is returned before any hop runs), hop 2 consults the global scope only when the gold returns null, and hops 3 and 4 pass the start scope and the name along; no hop sees which local scopes declare the name, so once the gold returns the outer of two local declarations no caller can recover the inner one without redoing the gold's walk. The gold's javadoc promises the variable that the name refers to in the local scopes searched from the given scope outward, i.e. the innermost declaration (lexical scoping); the variant returns the outermost. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the StaticScope.getSlot contract ('continues searching through parent scopes if a slot with this name is not found in the current scope'), the sibling implementation TightenTypes.ConcreteScope.getSlot (own slot, then parent.getSlot; first found wins) and Scope.isDeclared (own table, then the parent); ShadowVariablesTest::testShadowSimple2, VariableReferenceCheckTest::testCorrectShadowing and TypeCheckTest::testScoping1 (an own declaration shadows an enclosing one) and ScopedAliasesTest::testShadowedVar (a local declaration shadows a global one, through hop 2) pass on the variant.
